title: Cox's Bazar Sea Beach
description: Stretching over 120 kilometers unbroken along the Bay of Bengal, Cox's Bazar is the longest natural sea beach in the world. Famous for golden sand, sunset vistas at Kolatoli and Laboni beaches, and serene serenity at Inani Beach with its coral stones.

title: Saint Martin's Island & Chera Dwip
bnTitle: সেন্ট মার্টিন দ্বীপ ও ছেঁড়া দ্বীপ
description: Bangladesh's only coral island, located in the northeastern Bay of Bengal. Known for crystal-clear turquoise waters, coconut groves, live coral reefs, and the adjoining Chera Dwip that separates during high tide.

title: Sajek Valley (Kingdom of Clouds)
description: Perched at 1,800 feet above sea level in the Kasalong mountain range, Sajek Valley is famed for its ocean of drifting clouds, picturesque wooden resorts, Helipad vantage points, and vibrant indigenous Lushei and Tripura cultures.

title: Nilgiri & Bandarban Hill Peaks
description: One of the highest and most scenic hill stations in Bangladesh, Nilgiri offers a 360-degree panoramic view above the cloud blanket. Surrounding attractions include Chimbuk Hill, Shailopropat waterfall, and the mystical Boga Lake.

title: Sundarbans Mangrove Forest
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and the world's largest contiguous tidal halophytic mangrove forest. Habitat of the iconic Royal Bengal Tiger, saltwater crocodiles, spotted deer, and thousands of winding delta canals best explored via cruise.

title: Ratargul Freshwater Swamp Forest
description: The only freshwater swamp forest in Bangladesh and one of the few in South Asia. During the monsoon, the evergreen forest remains submerged under 20-30 feet of freshwater, creating a magical labyrinth navigated by traditional wooden dinghies.

title: Sreemangal Tea Gardens & Lawachara
description: Known as the Tea Capital of Bangladesh, Sreemangal boasts endless rolling green tea estates, the legendary 7-layer tea at Nilkantha Tea Cabin, rubber plantations, and the rich tropical biodiversity of Lawachara National Park.

title: Bisnakandi & Jaflong
description: Nestled right at the foot of Meghalaya's Khasi Hills, where gushing mountain streams meet clear stone-strewn rivers like the Piyain and Mari. Renowned for rolling mountain backdrops, fresh water streams, and Mayabi springs.

title: Tanguar Haor Wetland
description: A Ramsar Wetland site of international importance spanning Sunamganj. In monsoon, it transforms into an endless freshwater inland sea framed by the Meghalaya hills, best experienced while living aboard a traditional wooden houseboat (Bajra).

title: Kuakata Sea Beach (Sagor Konna)
description: Rare panoramic beach located in southern Bangladesh offering unobstructed views of both sunrise and sunset over the Bay of Bengal waters. Nearby sites include Gangamati Reserved Forest, the ancient Buddhist temple, and Fatrar Bon.

title: Kaptai Lake & Hanging Bridge
description: The largest man-made freshwater lake in South Asia, created on the Karnaphuli River. Surrounded by lush emerald hills, picturesque floating markets, Shuvolong waterfalls, and the scenic hanging bridge of Rangamati.

title: Somapura Mahavihara (Paharpur)
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site built by the Pala king Dharmapala in the 8th century. One of the most famous and largest Buddhist monastic complexes in the Indian subcontinent, featuring a magnificent central cruciform shrine.

title: Mahasthangarh Citadel
description: One of the earliest urban archaeological sites identified in Bangladesh, dating back to at least the 3rd century BCE as Pundranagara. Features ancient fortifications, Govinda Bhita, and historical relics along the Karatoya River.

title: Kantajew Terracotta Temple
description: Built in the 18th century by Maharaja Pran Nath, this late-medieval Hindu temple is celebrated for some of the finest terracotta relief work in Bengal, depicting scenes from the Mahabharata and Ramayana on every inch of its brick walls.

title: Lalbagh Fort & Old Dhaka Heritage
description: An incomplete 17th-century Mughal fort complex situated along the Buriganga River in Old Dhaka, commissioned by Mughal prince Muhammad Azam Shah. Houses the Tomb of Pari Bibi, the Diwan-i-Aam, and a Mughal-era mosque.

title: Ahsan Manzil (Pink Palace)
description: The official residential palace and seat of the Nawab of Dhaka, built in Indo-Saracenic revival architecture overlooking the Buriganga River. Today it serves as a national museum displaying artifacts of 19th-century royal life in Bengal.

title: Panam Nagar & Sonargaon
description: The ancient capital of Isa Khan and the Baro-Bhuiyans. Panam Nagar is a preserved ghost city consisting of dozens of European-influenced mansions built in the late 19th and early 20th centuries by wealthy Hindu merchants, alongside the Sonargaon Folk Art Museum.

title: Susang Durgapur (Birishiri)
description: Famed for its turquoise ceramic blue lake surrounded by gentle white clay hills, the pristine Someshwari River with its transparent waters, the Garo Baptist Mission, and indigenous Hajong cultural heritage at the foot of the Meghalaya border.

title: Sixty Dome Mosque (Shat Gombuj Masjid)
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site founded by Khan Jahan Ali in the 15th century Sultanate period. Despite its name, it features 77 low domes and four corner domes on an impressive Tughlaq-influenced brick architecture structure.

title: Boga Lake & Keokradong Trail
description: A natural, mysteriously deep freshwater lake formed in a volcanic crater or tectonic fault line around 1,200 feet above sea level in the deep hills of Ruma. The gateway for trekkers aiming to conquer Keokradong peak.
